title: The Story of a Life
publisher: Longman, Hurst, Rees, Orme, Brown, and Green
setting: Southampton, the New Forest, Portugal, France, Italy, North Africa, and the Red Sea
summary: Written by the British army officer and travel writer Joseph Moyle Sherer (1789–1869) as his first novel, and originally published anonymously in two volumes in 1825, The Story of a Life is framed around a manuscript left behind by an elderly stranger who settles in Southampton in 1790. Looking back thirty-five years, the narrator, Osman Beavoir, recounts leaving his father’s home in the New Forest for Portugal, surviving the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, and spending years wandering as a French parolee in Brest, a traveller in Italy, a captive in North Africa, and a fugitive across Naples, Egypt, and the Red Sea before returning to England in old age. Embedded within his account are four separate tales told by people he encounters along the way.
omitted_from_reading: The title page of Volume II is in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: Originally published anonymously in two volumes as by the author of “Scenes and Impressions in Egypt and Italy” and “Recollections of the Peninsula”; combined here into a single digital volume.

The printed novel has no numbered chapters; for readability, each volume is divided at natural scene breaks and embedded tales into sections in the reading editions (editorial section headings are distinguished from the four printed tale titles).

Original 1825 spellings, dialect, and transposed printed page numbers (pp. 31 and 30 on leaves p1038–p1039 in Volume II) are preserved as printed; repeated line-start quotation marks in a six-line song on p0131 are removed per modern convention, and thirty-four unmistakable printer’s errors are marked in the JSON and corrected in the reading editions.

Thirty-five pages in Volume II that triggered an automated recitation filter during primary drafting (p1022–p1023, p1050–p1055, p1069–p1070, p1108–p1109, p1120, p1141–p1142, p1263–p1264, p1311–p1317, and p1362–p1372) were drafted via local Tesseract OCR followed by page-by-page Gemini Pro corrections against the scan, then verified by Gemini Flash and included in the blind sampled audit.
